coordinates.object_orientation: Long axis X, head -X and tail +X, dorsal +Z, paired fins symmetric across Y. Front camera -Y gives broadside, side+X looks toward head, top+Z, perspective(+X,-Y,+Z).

concept.reason: Real whole fossil with scale plus documented same-species anatomical restoration suffice.

representation: Conservative whole living fish restoration, not a fossil slab and not an exact soft-tissue scan
primary_specimen: NHM London whole fossil in Parry2024 Fig3.5C; collection catalogue number not stated and unknown

context.age: Permian; species documented in Late Permian Marl Slate/Kupferschiefer
context.provenance_caution: Fig3.5C museum is named but precise specimen locality/catalogue number are not supplied; do not invent them.

scope: Original607 complete early coelacanth fish; preserve slender body, lobed paired fins, differentiated two dorsal fins and three-lobed tail. Do not substitute living Latimeria.

dimensions.basis: Length approximately600mm estimated from SAME Fig3.5C 6cm scale bar, uncertainty roughly +/-30mm; not a published caliper measurement. Body depth/width/fin envelope conservative living reconstruction inferences. Fossil laterally compressed. GCRFig10.11 reports species range63-600mm only for crosscheck, not the size of this specimen.

must_preserve: Elongate slender fish with relatively narrow elongated head and sizeable lateral eyes; head about30 percent length is working reconstruction.
Distinct anterior dorsal with ray-supported sail and NO fleshy lobe; posterior dorsal smaller with fleshy lobe.
Paired pectoral and pelvic fins with low fleshy lobes and ray-supported blades; separate posterior ventral anal fin.
Three-lobed caudal fin: upper and lower broad rounded lobes with short axial central terminal lobe. Not a forked teleost tail or long eel ribbon.
Median fins separated by body gaps; do not merge dorsal/anal into tail.
Closed or narrowly parted fish mouth, subtle opercular seam, no exposed skeleton or exaggerated teeth.
Subdued original inferred coloration; no modernLatimeria white speckles copied from Fig3.5A.
